To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(a) model-based offline RL is a promising direction for learning policies in real-world settings where data-collection policies are expensive, and (b) model-based offline approaches that explicitly optimize the data-collection policies can achieve better sample efficiency than existing approaches, while also achieving better deployment efficiency than naïvely applying existing approaches recursively.

(1) naïvely applying existing offline RL methods recursively is not sample efficient, and (2) our novel model-based offline RL method is both sample- and deployment-efficient, achieving impressive results on simulated robotic environments.

(1) we introduce a new notion of deployment efficiency for offline RL, (2) we propose a novel model based algorithm that is both sample efficient and achieves high deployment efficiency, and (3) we empirically demonstrate the efficacy of our algorithm on a variety of simulated robotics and control tasks.
